## Observed failure (hosted CI, not a new local reproduction)

At PR #24 head `d7f1e61b6d90add7ed2d61bc570278398f302198`, both Node 22 and Node 26 fail the existing test **“start refuses terminal lanes and rolls back newly acquired claims on Git or field failures”**, at `test/edges.test.ts:28:10`: expected `false`, actual `true`.

- [Node 22 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40462648873/job/122050615194)
- [Node 26 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40462648873/job/122050615276)
- [Exact test](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/d7f1e61b6d90add7ed2d61bc570278398f302198/test/edges.test.ts#L9-L29)

The Node 22 run reports 555 tests, 554 passing, 1 failing. This is the outer suite failure, not intentionally failing nested fixtures printed by tooling tests.

## Reproduction / expected behavior

Use the repository’s existing fixture and linked SDK setup, then run:

```sh
node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern="start refuses terminal lanes" test/edges.test.ts
```

The test creates a `PmClient({cwd, pmRoot, author:'swarm-test', noExtensions:true})`. After releasing the prior claim, `Swarm.start(id)` rejects, but a subsequent read still reports `claim_state.claimed === true`.

Expected: an unsuccessful start must release a claim newly acquired by that attempt. It must retain a pre-existing claim, and preserve genuinely intervening peer changes. Actual: the newly acquired claim remains held after the rejected start.

Impact: a caller receives a failed start with no usable lane while leaving the item assigned/claimed, potentially blocking another agent’s work.

## Static lead, not a proven root cause

[Current start cleanup/admission](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/d7f1e61b6d90add7ed2d61bc570278398f302198/src/swarm.ts#L147-L195) initializes `claimVersion` from the pre-claim version and advances it only in `onCommitted`; cleanup then uses that version in `releaseAcquiredClaim`. Check whether the no-extensions path supplies the same committed-document/version evidence before applying the stale-document guard. This is an inspection lead; the evidence above establishes the observable leak, not its complete causal chain.

## Canonical scope and deduplication

The existing [pm-swarm-y972 item](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/d7f1e61b6d90add7ed2d61bc570278398f302198/.agents/pm/features/pm-swarm-y972.toon) already includes this edge-test command and cleanup-preservation work. All-status issues and the current PM feature corpus were checked. This is distinct from #27’s close-after-handoff/reclaim refusal: this failure occurs during failed **start**, with a newly acquired claim.

## Acceptance / regression criteria

- The named existing test passes on Node 22 and Node 26, including both newly acquired and pre-existing claim cases.
- A rejected start leaves no newly owned claim, lane, or Git branch behind.
- Cleanup retains generation/document fencing: do not release a peer’s replacement claim or overwrite intervening content to make the test pass.
- The no-extensions refusal remains truthful; do not silently enable extensions.
- Re-run the existing acquisition-receipt/start-cleanup/peer-cleanup suites and full release gate, recording any remaining gaps.

Limits: this report relies on exact-head hosted test evidence plus static source analysis. No destructive, crash, permission, or concurrency fault-injection drills were run locally; no whole-release certification is implied.
